title: Multi-Agent Peer Conformity (Asch Consensus Trap in Agent Debates)

judge_reliability.protocol: Orthogonal 3-family jury with 2-shot anchored binary rubrics (zero self-judging)

if_then_decision_rules: IF orchestrating multi-agent code, SQL, or ops reviews on verifiable facts with November 2026 frontier models, skip anti-conformity prompt boilerplate: default postures already hold 100.0% ground against unanimous 3-0 wrong consensus (n = 240, alpha = 1.00).

IF auditing agent debate logs for peer-by-peer rebuttals, expect models to omit naming peers under unanimous error (7.5% citation rate; 0% on GPT-6.2 Sol, Gemini 4 Neon, and DeepSeek V4 Pro) while citing peers 55.0% overall (100.0% on Opus 5.5 and Qwen 4 Max) once a single dissenter speaks up; require explicit peer attribution in the prompt if audit logs need it.
IF routing DeepSeek V4 Pro into unanimous-disagreement debates, budget ~50% higher reasoning-token headroom (226.1 -> 330.6 mean tokens, and 369.5 under truth-anchor prompting).
limitations: All 8 traps tested verifiable technical facts with deterministic counterexamples; ambiguous architecture tradeoffs or multi-turn persuasion may yield higher conformity.
